euronews.title: Germany: Berlin student protest targets rearmament and compulsory service
euronews.description: Thousands of students marched through Berlin, on Friday 20 November 2026, protesting against the country's rapid military rearmament and fears of a return to compulsory military service. Their protest formed part of a wider wave of youth demonstrations across Europe.

euronews.title: Video shows dramatic helicopter rescue of woman trapped in flood channel
euronews.description: Los Angeles County firefighters rescued a woman trapped in a fast-moving flood control channel using a helicopter and an airborne paramedic.

euronews.title: Germany intensifies engagement with South Caucasus as 'region of opportunities'
euronews.description: Germany's foreign minister visited Azerbaijan and Armenia to develop projects of “strategic importance to Europe both economically and politically," in the context of Russia's aggression against Ukraine and the economic situation in Europe.

euronews.title: Trump defends Putin ties and accuses Iran of dishonesty in negotiations
euronews.description: Speaking at a White House following his trip to Asia, Trump defended his ties with Xi and Putin, claiming the Russian leader wanted to end the war in Ukraine through diplomacy. He also called for a "real deal" with Iran.

euronews.title: Thousands protest across Europe demanding better wages and services
euronews.description: Demonstrations began Friday in over 25 European countries and are expected to continue through the weekend as part of a coordinated international protest movement.

euronews.title: What do we know about Rwanda return hubs and how effective will they be?
euronews.description: Five EU countries have announced a controversial plan to set up a centre in Rwanda for migrants with no legal right to stay in Europe. While supporters say it will help governments to deter illegal immigration, critics are concerned about potential human rights violations and a lack of oversight.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: EU and UK strike post-Brexit reset deal as Russian missiles hit Poland
euronews.description: The EU and UK have struck a major post-Brexit reset deal in Brussels. In tonight’s edition of Europe Tonight, we bring you a live interview from the summit, assess security alarms after Russian missiles hit Poland, and examine the final-day standoff at COP31.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | November 20th, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 20th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Researchers find that cats tailor their communication to get human attention
euronews.description: A plaintive meow, a gentle purr or an innocent wide-eyed look: cats clearly know how to get their humans' attention. Scientific studies show that they use surprisingly sophisticated communication strategies.

euronews.title: Morocco commits €366 million to build a national defence industry by 2035
euronews.description: The royal cabinet said the plan aims to meet 40% of the armed forces’ and security services’ equipment needs through domestic production by 2035 and to generate more than 65% of industry revenues from exports, supported by a new strategic agency, a holding company, and two new industrial zones.

euronews.title: Spain requires data centres to draw 80% of their electricity from renewables
euronews.description: Spain tightens regulation of data centres with new requirements on renewable energy, efficiency and digital sovereignty to limit their impact on the power grid and attract sustainable investment.

euronews.title: France investigates suspected confidential leaks to Le Pen's far-right party
euronews.description: A former senior Interior Ministry official is suspected of sharing details of investigations into National Rally's election campaign finances, according a French newspaper.

euronews.title: Deepening EU–Canada ties: From critical minerals and defence to erasmus+
euronews.description: ‘We are determined to drive the renewed political momentum between the EU and Canada forward,’ write four Members of the European People’s Party (EPP) Group in the European Parliament in an op-ed for Euronews, published on the occasion of a visit by an EPP delegation to Canada on 19–21 November.

euronews.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
euronews.description: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

euronews.title: Italy: Workers and students stage nationwide strike over living costs
euronews.description: Workers and students marched through Rome, on Friday 20 November 2026, joining a nationwide strike over stagnant wages, rising living costs and government spending priorities. Protesters also demanded more funding for education and criticised military spending.

euronews.title: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh pledges ‘relentless diplomacy’ in bid to lead the UN
euronews.description: Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati star diplomat running to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development, and prosperity. She has pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.

euronews.title: From Tashkent to Amman: Books and Universities Bring Uzbekistan and Jordan Closer Together
euronews.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan deepen ties through book launches, academic conferences and university partnerships, highlighting reforms and shared cultural heritage.

euronews.title: EU Commission partially clears Hungary’s €10bn recovery fund payment after rule of law reforms
euronews.description: The European Commission says Budapest has met all but one of the conditions for the full €10bn payment. The financial penalty for the missing milestone is expected to be “minimal”, sources told Euronews.

rfi.title: Cost of living protests set to continue across Europe over weekend
rfi.description: Protests across Europe against conditions in schools, housing and the soaring cost of living are set to continue throughout the weekend, with hundreds of thousands expected to take to the streets in countries across the continent – including France, Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom.

rfi.title: UN climate talks run into overtime as countries clash over fossil fuel cuts
rfi.description: Deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial support for poorer nations pushed the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey beyond its scheduled closing day on Friday, as nearly 200 countries struggled to agree on how to tackle global warming.

rfi.title: French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race
rfi.description: French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left.

rfi.title: Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set
rfi.description: Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

rfi.title: EU and UK agree 'landmark' deal at Burnham's Brussels summit
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials on Friday sealed deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.

rfi.title: France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally
rfi.description: France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.

rfi.title: Nigeria moves to end prison sentences for attempted suicide
rfi.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked the Nigerian parliament to decriminalise attempted ​suicide and provide support for people who have tried to take their own lives. The move is aimed at ​treating ‌suicide attempts as a ⁠mental health issue rather than a criminal offence, in a country where access to psychological healthcare is limited and suicidal thoughts are often treated as a spiritual affliction.

rfi.title: Africa accounts for half of world's children living in conflict zones, NGO warns
rfi.description: Around 260 million children in Africa were living close to armed conflict in 2025 – amounting to two in five, a larger proportion than ever previously recorded, the charity Save the Children said in a report on Thursday. Worldwide, nearly one in four children lived near fighting.

rfi.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya, says top UN court
rfi.description: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said on Thursday in an historic ruling, ordering refugees be given safe passage home and awarded compensation.

rfi.title: EU delays new methane emissions rules until 2029 despite climate concerns
rfi.description: The European Union has agreed to postpone new methane emissions regulations for two years, giving the oil and gas industry more time to adapt amid mounting pressure on global energy markets. But environmental groups warn the decision risks undermining climate ambitions.

rfi.title: Europe left out in the cold as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
rfi.description: As the leaders of the United States, China and Russia held historic talks in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday, representatives of the European Union – the world's largest trading bloc – were conspicuously absent, despite the fact the discussions could have far-reaching consequences for Europe.

rfi.title: France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe
rfi.description: France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.

rfi.title: Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax
rfi.description: The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians.

rfi.title: Mistral boss denies French AI firm is Macron's 'personal project'
rfi.description: The head of French artificial intelligence company Mistral has rejected claims that the firm was a "personal project" of President Emmanuel Macron, insisting that support for AI transcended political boundaries.

rfi.title: US mining group wins controversial Kenya critical minerals contract
rfi.description: American consortium Frontier Minerals on Thursday won the contract for a critical minerals mining project at Mrima Hill in Kenya, beating out Chinese and Australian firms.

rfi.title: Fiji declares nationwide disaster as El Nino drought reaches crisis levels
rfi.description: South Pacific nation Fiji has declared a national state of disaster as a drought fuelled by the El Nino weather phenomenon reaches "crisis" levels.

rfi.title: France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war
rfi.description: The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory.

rfi.title: OpenAI partners with NATO to strengthen alliance's cyber defences
rfi.description: OpenAI announced Tuesday that it is partnering with NATO to help the transatlantic alliance strengthen its cyber defences and investigate potential attacks.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’interpellation de Michel Zecler, le caractère raciste des violences retenu, trois policiers condamnés à des peines de prison ferme et l’espoir d’une « jurisprudence »
lemonde.description: Contrôlé en 2020 devant son studio de musique, le producteur avait été tabassé par les agents, qui avaient ensuite prétendu sur procès-verbal qu’il les avait agressés. Une version démentie par les images filmées par une caméra de surveillance.

lemonde.title: La loi sur la présomption de légitime défense pour les forces de l’ordre définitivement adoptée par le Parlement, ayant été approuvée au Sénat
lemonde.description: La gauche sénatoriale a d’ores et déjà annoncé qu’elle saisirait en commun le Conseil constitutionnel pour faire barrage à la promulgation de ce qu’elle considère comme l’instauration d’un « permis de tuer » pour les policiers.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Dominique de Villepin officialise sa candidature, entre geste gaullien et référence révolutionnaire
lemonde.description: Après le faux départ de 2012, l’ancien premier ministre entend bien être présent au premier tour en avril. A 73 ans, il se frottera peut-être pour la première fois au suffrage universel. Il a dévoilé vendredi ses premières propositions et livré un réquisitoire implacable contre les différents partis.

lemonde.title: Le Danemark accuse la Russie d’avoir commandité la tentative d’assassinat d’un rappeur ukrainien sur son territoire
lemonde.description: Selon Copenhague, les services de renseignements russes avaient planifié le meurtre d’Albert Vasiliev, alias Kyivstoner, en s’appuyant sur la participation du gang danois Loyal to Familia. Le chef de la diplomatie a annoncé ce 20 novembre l’expulsion de l’attaché militaire russe en poste au Danemark.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, Wall Street en déroute après la dégringolade des sociétés liées à l’intelligence artificielle
lemonde.description: Les inquiétudes sur le modèle économique des entreprises, les incertitudes sur l’avenir des data centers et les déboires du champion Nvidia ont effacé des milliards de dollars de valorisation, la Bourse américaine vivant une de ses pires semaines depuis la crise liée au Covid.

lemonde.title: Génocide des Rohingya : la Cour internationale de justice « confirme qu’elle est indubitablement la boussole du droit international »
lemonde.description: En reconnaissant le génocide des Rohingya commis par la Birmanie, la plus haute Cour de l’ONU établit pour la première fois la responsabilité d’un Etat dans « le crime des crimes ». Alors que l’Afrique du Sud a saisi l’institution contre Israël, accusant l’Etat hébreu d’un génocide contre les Palestiniens de Gaza, cet arrêt pourrait faire jurisprudence.

lemonde.title: Une information judiciaire ouverte contre Gérard Depardieu et Michel Houellebecq, accusés de viol en réunion et d’agressions sexuelles lors d’un tournage
lemonde.description: L’ouverture d’une « information judiciaire sur plainte » d’une comédienne ayant tourné dans un film en 2018 avec l’acteur et l’écrivain, a été confirmée par le parquet, vendredi.

lemonde.title: A Ribeauvillé, le maire refuse la pose d’un pavé de mémoire pour un ancien habitant juif
lemonde.description: La ville du Haut-Rhin appuie son refus en se défendant de ne pas vouloir favoriser une catégorie de victimes du nazisme. Des arguments sur lesquels s’interrogent la famille et l’association.

lemonde.title: Budget : députés et sénateurs s’entendent sur un premier texte malgré l’enlisement politique
lemonde.description: La commission mixte paritaire réunie vendredi 19 novembre a trouvé un accord sur le projet de loi de fin de gestion pour 2026. Trouver un compromis sur le budget 2027, rejeté à l’Assemblée et jugé « suicidaire » au Sénat, s’annonce plus ardu.

lemonde.title: « GTA VI » s’offre un lancement record avec 3,79 milliards de dollars de ventes dès le premier jour
lemonde.description: Ces revenus, équivalents à 3,5 milliards d’euros environ, sont près de cinq fois supérieurs à ceux générés en vingt-quatre heures par la version précédente de la mythique saga de « Grand Theft Auto », en 2013. Le jeu vidéo, lancé jeudi, a été salué par la critique.

lemonde.title: En Suisse aussi, la jeunesse descend dans la rue contre « un avenir bouché »
lemonde.description: Plusieurs dizaines de milliers de jeunes ont manifesté vendredi 20 novembre dans les grandes villes du pays alpin. Austérité budgétaire, coupes dans les services publics, pouvoir d’achat, coût du logement et crise climatique alimentaient les slogans.

lemonde.title: Projet de loi logement : les députés n’ont pas revoté sur le droit de louer les passoires thermiques
lemonde.description: L’examen de ce texte qui ambitionne de relancer la création de logements s’est achevé vendredi. Le gouvernement mise sur une suppression ultérieure de l’amendement RN qui réautorise la mise en location des logements les plus énergivores.

lemonde.title: Au Mali, une nouvelle société militaire turque épaule secrètement la junte d’Assimi Goïta
lemonde.description: Des instructeurs d’Equipped Tactical Academy ont formé des éléments des forces spéciales maliennes, fin 2025. Si la Russie reste, avec environ 2 000 militaires d’Africa Corps, le premier partenaire du Mali dans le secteur de la défense, la Turquie est également un allié sûr du pouvoir d’Assimi Goïta.

lemonde.title: « Inside Deutsche Bank » : le gouvernement allemand réclame de la « transparence » sur les révélations de l’enquête journalistique
lemonde.description: Ebranlée par les articles du consortium de plus de 50 médias, dont « Le Monde », l’institution allemande minimise des faits jugés anciens. Mais la chute en Bourse et l’indignation politique internationale maintiennent la pression sur l’établissement bancaire.

lemonde.title: Seine-Saint-Denis : le policier qui a tué un automobiliste en 2022 condamné à dix-huit mois de prison ferme sans mandat de dépôt
lemonde.description: L’avocate générale avait demandé cinq ans de réclusion criminelle, assortis d’un mandat de dépôt différé, à l’encontre de cet ancien brigadier-chef de la BAC.

lemonde.title: Incendies de Los Angeles : un suspect reconnu coupable, après un deuxième procès
lemonde.description: Jonathan Rinderknecht était accusé d’être à l’origine d’un feu que les pompiers pensaient initialement avoir éteint mais qui a finalement repris, le 7 janvier 2025, et a ravagé le quartier huppé de Pacific Palisades.

zeit.title: »Grand Theft Auto«: »GTA VI« spielt Rekordumsatz von 3,8 Milliarden US-Dollar ein
zeit.description: Der Start des Videospiels »GTA VI« wurde von Fans mit großer Spannung erwartet. Am ersten Verkaufstag sprengt der Titel gleich eine Reihe von Rekorden.

zeit.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Anthropic-Forscher will mathematisches Millennium-Problem gelöst haben
zeit.description: Mithilfe der KI Claude habe er einen Beweis der Riemannschen Vermutung gefunden, schreibt ein Anthropic-Mitarbeiter. Ein führender Mathematiker zeigt sich begeistert.

zeit.title: Demonstrationen: Festnahmen und fliegende Flaschen nach Jugendprotesten
Demonstrationen: Frankfurter Jugendproteste bleiben trotz Warnungen friedlich
Verheerende Feuer: Prozess um Palisades-Feuer in LA: Mann schuldig gesprochen
Jugendproteste: Randale überschatten «Gen Z regelt»-Demo in Hamburg
Gen-Z-Proteste: Wird das noch eine Bewegung?
zeit.description: Zum zweiten Mal in drei Wochen sind bundesweit Zehntausende junge Menschen auf die Straße gegangen. Ihre Ziele bleiben diffus. Wird sich der Protest dennoch verstetigen?

zeit.title: Gen Z regelt: Gen-Z-Proteste beendet – Demonstrationsgeschehen überwiegend friedlich
zeit.description: Bundesweit haben Zehntausende an Jugendprotesten teilgenommen. Trotz einiger Zusammenstöße verliefen die Demonstrationen insgesamt friedlich. Das Liveblog zum Nachlesen

zeit.title: Umwelt: Ausfuhrstopp für Plastikmüll aus der EU in viele Länder
Nach Ärger bei Konzert: Städtetags-Präsident kritisiert Tokio Hotel scharf
Prozess in Frankreich: Haftstrafen für französische Polizisten wegen Gewalt gegen Schwarzen
zeit.description: Vor sechs Jahren verprügelten drei Pariser Polizisten einen Schwarzen Musikproduzenten. Anschließend versuchten sie, die Tat zu vertuschen. Nun fiel das Urteil.

zeit.title: Börsengang in den USA: Anthropic-Aktie rutscht am zweiten Handelstag deutlich ab
zeit.description: Der KI-Anbieter Anthropic schaffte den wertvollsten Börsengang aller Zeiten. Doch am Tag darauf erlebte der Konzern einen Ausverkauf, der die gesamten US-Börsen erfasste.

zeit.title: Bundesregierung: Juso-Chef Türmer kritisiert Koalition wegen Stromsteuersenkung
zeit.description: Philipp Türmer sieht in der Stromsteuersenkung eine »Entlastungsmaßnahme für den Kanzler«. Der Juso-Chef hätte lieber eine Verkürzung der gesetzlichen Arbeitszeit.

zeit.title: Schulstreiks: Demos gegen Wehrpflicht in Rheinland-Pfalz und Saarland
Interesse geringer: Hier ging die Jugend auf die Straße – und so lief es

nzz.title: Die KI-Branche zieht einen weiteren rabenschwarzen Börsentag ein: Nvidia verliert 14 Prozent an Marktwert
nzz.description: Auch Anthropic wird am zweiten Tag nach seinem erfolgreichen IPO abgestraft. Die Sorgen an der Börse wiegen schwer, dass die KI-Unternehmen niemals so profitabel werden könnten, wie man sich das erhofft.

nzz.title: «Eine Schande!» oder «Eine interessante Erfahrung»? Das Ticket der SVP erzählt einiges über die Partei und ihre Gesichter
nzz.description: Episoden eines Abends, über dessen Protagonisten in Bern noch länger geredet wird.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Jugendstreik in Europa: Die Demonstrationen haben sich aufgelöst – die Polizei zieht nun Bilanz
nzz.description: Für den 20. November haben Jugendliche zu Protesten aufgerufen. Die NZZ berichtet live aus Zürich, Bern, der Westschweiz, Paris, Rom und Berlin.

nzz.title: Nachfolge von Guy Parmelin im Bundesrat: Die SVP nominiert Thomas Aeschi und Michael Graber
nzz.description: Die Bundeshausfraktion der SVP präsentiert dem Parlament ein Zweierticket.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Der Entscheid ist gefallen: Die SVP nominiert Thomas Aeschi und Michael Graber für den Bundesrat
nzz.description: Fraktionschef Thomas Aeschi gilt als gesetzt, doch neben ihm bewerben sich sechs weitere Kandidaten und eine Kandidatin.

nzz.title: «Hoffnung am Horizont der Jugend»: Burnham zelebriert die Annäherung an die EU – und verschweigt die strittigen Punkte
nzz.description: Der britische Premierminister will die Brexit-Verwerfungen glätten und sieht sich von der Bevölkerung getragen. Um Widerspruch zu hören, musste er nicht weit reisen: Auch der Ukip-Chef Farage war nach Brüssel gepilgert.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Die USA nach den Midterms: Aussenminister Rubio verteidigt Trumps Treffen mit Xi und Putin
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus den USA während der zweiten Amtszeit von Präsident Donald Trump.

nzz.title: Zwei russische Marschflugkörper schlagen in Polen ein – die Regierung glaubt nicht an ein Versehen
nzz.description: Erstmals verletzt Russland den polnischen Luftraum in so grossem Ausmass. Der polnische Regierungschef Donald Tusk spricht von einer gezielten Provokation des Kremls.

nzz.title: Überdeckt der Rekord-Börsengang von Anthropic tieferliegende Probleme? Der KI-Pessimismus erfasst die Aktienmärkte
nzz.description: Bedenken über Ertragskraft und Verschuldung der Techkonzerne lösen eine Verkaufswelle aus. Die Frage, ob eine Spekulationsblase nun platzt, bleibt umstritten.

nzz.title: Neue Angriffswelle: Russland nimmt Kiews Brücken ins Visier
nzz.description: Seit einigen Wochen greift Russland gezielt die Dnipro-Übergänge in der Hauptstadt an, in der vergangenen Nacht erneut. Bis jetzt halten die Brücken stand, doch die Gefahr ist eine andere.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Berichte über Raketenangriff im Süden Irans
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Generalstreik und Jugenddemonstration in einem: Italiens grosser Protesttag
nzz.description: Die Opposition will von der breiten Mobilisierung gegen die Regierung profitieren. Doch sie kann nicht verbergen, dass sie in vielen wesentlichen Fragen uneins ist.

nzz.title: Schweizer Tourist bei Elefantenangriff in Kamerun getötet
nzz.description: Beim Abstieg von einer Bergtour am Mount Cameroon nutzt eine Touristengruppe einen Wanderpfad von Elefanten. Die Begegnung mit den Tieren endet für einen Wanderer tödlich.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Tausende Junge protestieren in Europa – die Bilder
nzz.description: Ob gegen Wehrpflicht in Deutschland, für bessere Bildung in Frankreich oder gegen Sparbudgets in Italien: Tausende junge Menschen haben am Freitag in europäischen Grossstädten ihre Stimme erhoben.

nzz.title: Hype um Anthropic verfliegt: Aktie schmiert kurz nach Rekord-Börsengang ab
nzz.description: Zweifel an der hohen Bewertung lassen den Hype um Anthropic schnell abebben.

france24fr.title: Mission Volia : la France en guerre contre la Russie ?
france24fr.description: Selon les révélations de nos confrères de RFI, des soldats français sont présents sur le sol ukrainien. Cela signifie-t-il que la France est en guerre contre la Russie? Le Général Michel Yakovleff nous donne son point de vue.

france24fr.title: Procès Zecler : les trois policiers condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme
france24fr.description: Les trois policiers ayant passé à tabac le producteur de musique noir Michel Zecler en 2020 ont été condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme. L'accusation avait de son côté requis, jeudi, entre quatre et six ans de prison ferme.

france24fr.title: Guinée/Burkina Faso: tensions après la diffusion de caricatures de M. Doumbouya
france24fr.description: Les tensions montent entre la Guinée et le Burkina Faso. Conakry vient de couper le signal de la RTB, la télévision publique burkinabè. En cause : un éditorial critique, avec une caricature du président Mamadi Doumbouya. Mais l'affaire va bien au-delà de la télé : elle éclate en pleine répression contre l'orpaillage illégal en Guinée, qui a déjà forcé des dizaines de milliers de Burkinabè à rentrer au pays.

france24fr.title: Valise nucléaire de Poutine : la mise en scène calculée du Kremlin
france24fr.description: Une vidéo largement relayée ces deux derniers jours montre l’aide de camp de Vladimir Poutine porter la valise nucléaire en marge de la rencontre trilatérale en Chine. Une séquence authentique mise en avant par la Russie pour menacer directement les alliés de l’Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Johann Chapoutot : "la dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"
france24fr.description: A 5 mois de la présidentielle en France, le RN domine toujours dans les sondages. Longtemps considéré comme anti républicain, infréquentable, il est désormais aux portes du pouvoir. Comment comprendre cette progression? Quelle est la responsabilité de la classe politique dans cette évolution? Quelles conséquences sur notre démocratie? Johann Chapoutot, Professeur d'Histoire contemporaine, auteur de "La bascule, Allemagne 1933" (éditions Gallimard), était l'Invité d'Au Coeur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Ligue des nations : la France de Zinedine Zidane face à la montagne espagnole
france24fr.description: La France affrontera l'Espagne en quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations, un défi XXL pour les Bleus face aux champions du monde en titre. Zinedine Zidane aura-t-il la recette pour enfin vaincre la "Roja" ?

france24fr.title: Sommet de Shenzhen, guerre en Ukraine, hostilités dans le Golfe
france24fr.description: Au sommaire de l'émission ce soir: la rencontre historique entre Xi Jinping, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump en marge du sommet de l'APEC; la guerre en Ukraine et les révélations de nos confrères de RFI sur la présence de soldats français sur le sol ukrainien, et le regain de tensions dans la guerre au Moyen-Orient, entre frappes iraniennes et offensive des Houthis au Yémen.

france24fr.title: Police : la loi sur la présomption de légitime défense définitivement adoptée par le Parlement
france24fr.description: Vivement combattue dans la rue par ses opposants qui l'assimilent à un "permis de tuer", l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre a été définitivement adoptée au Parlement vendredi soir, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale.

france24fr.title: Sans Starlink, l'Ukraine à l'assaut du pont de Crimée avec des drones relais
france24fr.description: Les frappes ukrainiennes contre le pont de Crimée depuis le 15 novembre ont été saluées comme un succès opérationnel majeur par l'Ukraine. Elles ont été facilitées par ce que le Financial Times a appelé des "modems volants", c'est-à-dire des drones relais de communication permettant de palier les limites de Starlink. Une technique méconnue mais de plus en plus en vogue sur le front ukrainien.

france24fr.title: Camille Lellouche, 360 degrés de talents
france24fr.description: Rendez-vous avec l'artiste pluridisciplinaire Camille Lellouche à l'occasion de la sortie de son nouvel album "Minuit". Autrice, compositrice, musicienne, chanteuse, humoriste et comédienne, elle revient sur son enfance à Vitry-sur-Seine, en banlieue parisienne, ses influences musicales – de la Mafia K'1 Fry aux valses de Chopin –, mais aussi sur la pugnacité et l'endurance nécessaires pour imposer sa liberté créative.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : l'hippopotame star du zoo de Cincinnati est morte
france24fr.description: Fiona, l’hippopotame star du zoo de Cincinnati dans l’Ohio (États-Unis), est morte le 19 novembre après avoir mangé un bonnet accidentellement tombé dans son enclos. La femelle âgé de 9 ans n’a pas survécu malgré les soins prodigués par les équipes vétérinaires.

france24fr.title: Boom de l'intelligence artificielle : la révolution à quel prix ?
france24fr.description: L'entrée en Bourse spectaculaire d'Anthropic n'aura pas suffi à dissiper les inquiétudes des marchés financiers. Rentabilité incertaine, turbulences chez Nvidia, contestation des centres de données... derrière les promesses de l'intelligence artificielle, les premières limites apparaissent.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Rencontre Trump, Poutine et Xi : suivez la conférence de presse du président américain
Mobilisations : la jeunesse européenne en colère
france24fr.description: À travers l'Europe, des jeunes d'une vingtaine de pays s'apprêtent à descendre dans la rue vendredi 20 novembre et ce week-end pour une grève internationale sous le mot d'ordre "Battez-vous pour notre avenir, pas pour leurs guerres".

france24fr.title: Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires
france24fr.description: Le parquet de Paris soupçonne l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, d'avoir informé le Rassemblement national sur des enquêtes judiciaires visant le parti. Une affaire qui illustre l'influence grandissante du parti lepéniste dans les hautes sphères de l'État.

france24fr.title: Salvador : Nayib Bukele, autoproclamé “dictateur le plus cool du monde”, brigue un troisième mandat.
france24fr.description: Le président de droite du Salvador, Nayib Bukele, a déposé jeudi 19 novembre au soir sa candidature pour un troisième mandat. Le Salvador, ayant modifié sa Constitution l'an dernier pour abolir la limite du nombre de mandats présidentiels, permet au candidat de se représenter à nouveau.

france24fr.title: Hubert Védrine : "Ce sommet Poutine-Xi-Trump est humiliant pour l'UE, mais sans décision concrète"
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, Caroline De Camaret reçoit Hubert Védrine, ancien secrétaire général de l'Élysée sous la présidence de François Mitterrand et ancien ministre socialiste des Affaires étrangères du gouvernement de Lionel Jospin. À l'occasion de la sortie de son ouvrage "2027, le rendez-vous du courage ?" (éditions Plon), il revient sur l'impuissance de l'Europe sur la scène internationale, sur la question migratoire et sur le sens à donner à la construction européenne depuis sa perspective gaullo-m

france24fr.title: Législatives anticipées en Espagne : Pedro Sánchez en danger ?
france24fr.description: Le 29 novembre, les regards du Parlement européen se tourneront du côté de l'Espagne, où sont organisées des élections législatives anticipées. Au pouvoir depuis 2018, le Premier ministre socialiste espagnol Pedro Sánchez a décidé, le mois dernier, de dissoudre le Parlement après le rejet de son projet de loi pour favoriser l'accès au logement.

observador.title: As notícias da 1h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: As peripécias da cobertura do julgamento de Duarte Lima
observador.description: Do comissário da polícia avisado em cima da hora para depor, ao juiz que se queixa dos telemóveis e dos “ácaros”: o que testemunham os jornalistas que estão a cobrir o julgamento de Duarte Lima.

observador.title: GTA VI bate recordes com 3,45 mil milhões de euros no dia 1
observador.description: A Rockstar Games confirmou números históricos para o regresso da franquia após 13 anos: o novo GTA partiu todos os recordes de pré-vendas e de faturação no primeiro dia em todas as plataformas.

observador.title: Neves promete aumentos salariais para PSP e GNR
observador.description: Luís Neves explicou que o entendimento prevê alterações em dois índices remuneratórios, um dos quais terá efeitos já em janeiro de 2027 e o segundo em janeiro de 2028.

observador.title: Tupanciretã. Forte tempestade causa 3 mortos e 60 feridos
observador.description: A cidade de Tupanciretã foi arrasada esta madrugada na sequência de uma tempestade acompanhada de granizo e ventos fortes, provocando três mortes, 60 feridos e cortes na energia, água e comunicação.

observador.title: Estudantes da FAL "satisfeitos" com congelamento de propinas
observador.description: Presidente da FAL instou o executivo a "não insistir" mais na questão, relembrando que a discussão deve passar sobretuo pela habitação, saúde mental e integração de novos estudantes.

observador.title: "Estamos todos com o Francisco. Somos uma família"
observador.description: Francisco Moura fez autogolo, chorou, pediu para sair e acabou consolado por colegas, adversários e adeptos. Farioli não escondeu "infelicidade", mas deixou mensagem de apoio total ao jovem lateral.

observador.title: Um político muito orgulhoso do “rouba, mas faz”
observador.description: Mandou numa das cidades mais prósperas do país, foi acusado de corrupção, formou um partido político e tentou vencer uma eleição nacional — mas falhou. Calma, estou a falar de Adhemar de Barros.

observador.title: Os selvagens 5G
observador.description: Quando alguém nasce, nasce selvagem, rezava a cantilena. Alguns crescem selvagens, e tão distantes de qualquer vestígio de decência que começa a ser embaraçoso reconhecê-los como nossos semelhantes.

observador.title: Todos, todos, todos... para, como e com Cristo!
observador.description: Que as vossas vidas sejam como páginas do Evangelho, escritas com a tinta da misericórdia, para que todos possam reconhecer em vós o amor e a alegria de Jesus!

observador.title: Entendam-se
observador.description: Amanhã, a Assembleia da República vota o Orçamento do Estado para 2027. Já não é o orçamento do Governo nem do PS. É de uma maioria que ninguém elegeu e que ninguém assume: a do PS com o Chega

observador.title: Plano Nocional de Leitura (LIII)
observador.description: Macedo tomava a sério a definição conhecida do “incomparável Buffon”: o estilo é o próprio homem.   Quando deplorava um deplorava o outro.

observador.title: Plano Nacional de Emergência para a Habitação (i)
observador.description: Se houver ousadia do actual Governo, se houver seriedade por parte da oposição, podemos fazer da habitação um desígnio nacional e avançar com um Plano Nacional de Emergência para a Habitação.

observador.title: "PS e Chega não sabem o que estão a fazer", acusa Montenegro
observador.description: Em Oliveira de Frades, o primeiro-ministro criticou PS e Chega por inviabilizarem medidas como o aumento das propinas, defendendo que seria oportunidade de investimento no ensino.

observador.title: Pequenos Cupidos e a mais serena das virtudes
observador.description: Uma ligeira inclinação da cabeça, a mão que afasta os cabelos, a luz sobre um ombro quando alguém se volta. Tão pouco. E, nesse tão pouco, a vida inteira perde o chão.

observador.title: Guerra moral pela escola: artistas, ignorância e sociopatia
observador.description: Decida o inconciliável: teimar na Epifania Moral da Solidariedade, legado da década de 1980 de Lawrence Kohlberg, ou assumir a Ordem Moral da Escada, tradição milenar revitalizada por Jordan Peterson.

observador.title: O novo partido de Isaltino: muito barulho por nada
observador.description: Isaltino, que após querelas abandonou em rutura o PSD em 2005, pode procurar um ato muito humano, demasiadamente humano – a vendetta.

observador.title: O debate entre Pedro Sánchez e Alberto Feijóo
observador.description: A poucos dias das eleições gerais em Espanha, o debate televisivo entre os dois principais candidatos trouxe tensão, ataques mútuos, mas manteve aberto a decisão para o dia 29 de novembro

spiegel.title: Kalifornien: Schuldspruch im Prozess um Palisades-Feuer in Los Angeles
spiegel.description: Ein Funke am Neujahrstag, aus dem eine Katastrophe wurde: Im Prozess um den mutmaßlichen Brandstifter in Los Angeles fällt ein Schuldspruch. Wie die Anklage ihren Verdacht begründet, zeigt sich im Detail.

spiegel.title: Verbrenner-Aus: Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger fordert Bekenntnis zu Deutschland
spiegel.description: Die EU könnte Autobauern erlauben, auch nach 2035 neue Verbrenner und Hybride zu verkaufen. Verkehrsminister Bilger knüpft daran eine klare Erwartung an die Hersteller.

spiegel.title: Jamal Musiala: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge bringt möglichen Gehaltsverzicht ins Spiel
spiegel.description: Jamal Musiala hat beim FC Bayern einen Vertrag bis 2030, fällt aber oft aus. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge hat nun öffentlich bezweifelt, dass der Offensivstar sein früheres Leistungsniveau wieder erreicht.

spiegel.title: GTA 6 spielt am ersten Verkaufstag knapp 3,8 Milliarden Dollar ein
spiegel.description: Das lang ersehnte Videospiel »GTA 6« hat nicht nur bei den Produktionskosten Rekorde gebrochen. Nun hat das Studio Rockstar Games die gewaltigen Verkaufszahlen vom Debüttag veröffentlicht.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Ex-Präsident Jair Bolsonaro wegen Bauchschmerzen im Krankenhaus
spiegel.description: Brasiliens Ex-Präsident Jair Bolsonaro ist seinem Sohn Carlos zufolge erneut im Krankenhaus. Der 71-Jährige musste Anfang des Jahres bereits behandelt werden. Sein Sohn unterstellt dem Staat Tötungsabsichten.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München: Verletzungssorgen nach Köln-Spiel – Kane und Olise angeschlagen
spiegel.description: Die Rückkehr von Trainer Vincent Kompany und Jamal Musiala sollte das Bundesliga-Heimspiel gegen den 1. FC Köln zum Fest machen. Stattdessen erlebten die Bayern einen Abend voller Frust.

spiegel.title: Alaska: Trächtiger Finnwal von Kreuzfahrtschiff getötet
spiegel.description: Ein Finnwalweibchen ist vor der Küste Alaskas mit einem Kreuzfahrtschiff kollidiert und gestorben – mitsamt seinem ungeborenen Kalb. Die Meeresgiganten gelten als stark gefährdet.

spiegel.title: Tom Brady steigt offenbar beim FC Chelsea ein
spiegel.description: Als Quarterback schrieb Tom Brady Sportgeschichte. Jetzt will sich der einstige Football-Star im Fußball verewigen: als Anteilseigner des FC Chelsea.

spiegel.title: Nvidia: US-Börsenaufsicht ermittelt gegen Chip-Riesen
spiegel.description: Der Techkonzern Nvidia rutscht immer tiefer in die Krise. Nach dem Skandal um Jensen Huang untersucht die US-Börsenaufsicht nun offenbar mutmaßliche Bilanzprobleme. Bekannt werden auch neue Details über seine Geliebte.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bank: Als Hacker aus China in das Geldhaus eindrangen
spiegel.description: Zehn Jahre lang blieb es geheim: Die Deutsche Bank war Ziel eines der gravierendsten Hackerangriffe der Geschichte. Interne Unterlagen zeigen jetzt, wie überfordert das Geldhaus agierte.

spiegel.title: Melania Trump bei Amazon Prime: Neue Serie über ihr hartes Leben als First Lady
spiegel.description: Zuerst der Kinofilm, nun die zweiteilige Serie: First Lady Melania Trump zeigt sich ungewollt unverstellt. Für Zuschauer ist dieses Bonusmaterial eine Offenbarung.

spiegel.title: Genozid-Urteil: Was die Entscheidung des Weltgerichts in Den Haag für Israel bedeutet
spiegel.description: Der Internationale Gerichtshof stuft Myanmars Gräueltaten an den Rohingya als Völkermord ein. Der Völkerrechtler Kai Ambos sagt, warum die Richter so entschieden haben – und was das für das Gaza-Verfahren bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Hugendubel ist offline: Hacker legen Onlineshop des Buchhändlers lahm
spiegel.description: Keine E-Books, keine Mails, kein Service: Die Internetseite der Buchhandelskette Hugendubel ist offline, offenbar wegen eines Hackerangriffs.

spiegel.title: Daniel Thomas: Britischer Rechtsextremist schlitzte Flüchtlingsboot auf – 15 Monate Haft
spiegel.description: Als Seenotretter im Ärmelkanal Menschen von einem Schlauchboot holten, schlitzte Rechtsextremist Daniel Thomas das Boot auf. Ein Richter nennt ihn nun einen »Aufmerksamkeitshascher« und verurteilt ihn zu einer Freiheitsstrafe.

spiegel.title: »Gen Z regelt«: Demos gehen zu Ende – das war der Protesttag in Europa
spiegel.description: Die allermeisten Demonstrationen in den Großstädten sind vorbei. Der Zulauf war geringer als noch vor drei Wochen. Bis zum Abend kam es nur vereinzelt zu Auseinandersetzungen mit der Polizei. Die Entwicklungen im Minutenprotokoll.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump will US-Konzernen verbieten, Rechenzentren im Ausland zu bauen
spiegel.description: US-Bürger protestieren zusehends gegen den Bau von KI-Rechenzentren. Weichen die großen Unternehmen ins Ausland aus? Präsident Trump droht den Konzernen.

spiegel.title: Lana Nusseibeh: Warum diese Frau die Uno nicht führen kann
spiegel.description: Es wäre Zeit für eine Frau an der Spitze der Uno. Doch die Kandidatin Lana Nusseibeh aus den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten hat ein großes Handicap.

spiegel.title: Andy Burnham und die EU: In Brüssel wird wieder die britische Nationalhymne gespielt
spiegel.description: Zehn Jahre nach dem Brexit-Referendum gehen die Briten unter Premier Burnham und die EU aufeinander zu – in kleinen Schritten. Vor allem Studierende dürfen sich freuen.

phys-org.title: Broadening the role of RNA: A messenger, a mediator and now a condensate coordinator
phys-org.description: New research about condensates—cellular compartments that act as hubs for facilitating biological reactions—continues to reveal novel insights into how cells function. Among those continuing to push the field forward are members of the Marine Biological Laboratory's condensate consortium, including Amy Gladfelter, a professor at Duke University and current co-director of the MBL physiology course, and former MBL physiology course student and past MBL Whitman fellow Dragomir Milovanovic, a p

phys-org.title: 'Forever' chemicals? Don't be so sure, says engineer
phys-org.description: Inside the disinfection room of Baltimore's Ashburton water filtration plant, 14 University of Maryland students clad in hard hats peered up at six towering vats of bleach used to treat water that flows from the distant Liberty Reservoir into the facility, killing bacteria and other pathogens before it's routed to the region's kitchen sinks.

phys-org.title: A fish as old as Montana—the blue sucker discovered to live well over 100 years
phys-org.description: Using bomb radiocarbon dating on microscopic otoliths (earstones), researchers have found that a native species of fish in the Upper Missouri River in Montana is living up to 130 years—more than triple the previous estimate of around 40 years—and some blue suckers alive today hatched in the late 1800s, around the dawn of the automobile and when Montana officially became a state.

phys-org.title: Caribbean corals are in crisis. Fossil reefs can help point to where corals may persist
phys-org.description: The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation.

phys-org.title: Ancient bison hunting site in Texas challenges long-held assumptions
phys-org.description: For decades, archaeologists questioned whether Native American communities in the Southern Plains hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, a sophisticated technique widely documented farther north.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover twist-tunable interlayer excitons in atomically thin anisotropic semiconductors
phys-org.description: When light shines on a semiconductor, negatively charged electrons and positively charged holes—empty states left behind when electrons move away—pair up and bind together. This bound state is called an exciton. When two atomically thin semiconductor layers are stacked, electrons and holes can reside in different layers, forming what is known as an interlayer exciton (IE).

phys-org.title: Gamified mobile payment features may drive adoption among Gen-Z users
phys-org.description: Gamified features in mobile payment applications may significantly increase adoption among consumers in emerging economies, with men and women responding in almost identical ways, according to research published in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.

phys-org.title: Record-setting X-ray laser reliably generates flashes with wavelengths shorter than distances between atoms
phys-org.description: Researchers from DESY and European XFEL have demonstrated reliable production and transport of X-ray laser flashes with a wavelength of about 0.04 nanometers (or a photon energy of 30,000 electronvolts) at European XFEL, raising their own world record. This means that the X-ray's wavelength is much shorter than typical distances between neighboring atoms in solids, which enables the study of materials with higher spatial resolution than before.

phys-org.title: Digital imaging workshop aims to reveal secrets in medieval manuscripts
phys-org.description: Researchers recently used multispectral imaging technology to try to uncover hidden information from medieval manuscripts at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The library hosted a digital imaging workshop in early October that served as a pilot study for how the technology can help analyze fragile, centuries-old documents.

phys-org.title: New hemp plant produces no detectable THC, potentially reducing risk of crop destruction
phys-org.description: Scientists at Texas A&M AgriLife Research, a member of The Texas A&M University System, have developed a hemp plant that produces no detectable cannabinoids, including THC.

phys-org.title: Tested on mushrooms, an AI model shows potential for detecting crop stress with far fewer computations
phys-org.description: A new artificial intelligence (AI) model can detect stress in agricultural crops using a nondestructive imaging technique, allowing changes in crop health to be monitored over time. Developed by a team of researchers at Penn State, the new model shows promise for accurately detecting crop stress caused by drought, disease, nutrient deficiency and other causes while using less computing power than some existing AI methods.

phys-org.title: Can Instagram reduce prejudice? Study reveals the potential and limits of social media contact
phys-org.description: A research team at the University of Potsdam has conducted a field experiment to investigate whether contact through social media can reduce prejudice. The findings suggest that following an unfamiliar Instagram profile for just three days can lead to more favorable attitudes—not only toward the group represented by the profile. The study was published in the Journal of the Association for Information Systems.

phys-org.title: A million tiny crystals reveal how semiconductors form distinct cores and shells
phys-org.description: Perovskites and related materials called perovskitoids are promising semiconductor materials for solar cells, LEDs and light detectors. Their ingredients and internal crystal structures determine how they absorb and emit light. A chip just 2 centimeters across can hold roughly a million tiny crystals—becoming a miniature material library that can show how some mixtures separate into distinct cores and shells, changing the light they absorb.

phys-org.title: Hazardous glacial lakes need reservoir-style safety oversight, says researcher
phys-org.description: As the climate warms, thousands of glacial lakes are growing behind potentially unstable natural dams. Despite the potential risk of flooding to communities downstream, these lakes remain outside formal safety regulation.

phys-org.title: People wade through floodwater because they underestimate danger—how to avoid risk
phys-org.description: A footpath home disappears beneath brown water. The other side is only a few meters away and someone has already crossed. Turning back means a long detour and you will be late. Would you wade through? This is the kind of everyday decision that flood safety advice must address.

phys-org.title: Global analysis reveals how lakes amplify glacier ice loss
phys-org.description: Glacial lakes can accelerate the retreat of glaciers. If glaciers border a lake, the water can melt the ice from underneath; furthermore, chunks of ice can break off and fall into the lake. The extent to which these processes influence the situation, compared with other factors, had not been sufficiently clarified at a global level until now.

phys-org.title: X-ray technique advances temperature measurements under extreme pressure
phys-org.description: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have advanced the ability to measure temperatures in materials subjected to extreme pressures at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), providing new insights into how materials behave under conditions relevant to national security and high-energy-density physics.

phys-org.title: Parasite protein expands understanding of how mitochondria build their ribosomes
phys-org.description: Mitochondria are essential components of the cells of most organisms, including humans. They are often referred to as the cell's powerhouses because they produce the energy needed for cellular functions. However, mitochondria originally evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells in the distant past.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem.
